- Support individuals subject to DoLS and other restrictions while maintaining their dignity, rights and independence.
- Support individuals with complex communication needs using simple language, visual aids, structured choices and other agreed communication strategies.
- Provide support with personal care, daily living activities, meals, medication, community access and meaningful activities as required.
- Maintain professional boundaries while developing positive and trusting relationships.
- Accurately record care delivery, behavioral observations, incidents, restrictive interventions and other significant events.

Work Style: Flexible working between home, office, and other suitable locations across the Black Country region, including the Office (Hickman Avenue, Wolverhampton)
Hours: 37 hours per week, Monday to Friday
Role type: Temporary
Pay Rate: 15.56 per hour

Make a Real Difference in the Lives of Children and Families

Are you passionate about supporting children and helping families thrive? Do you have experience working with children, young people, or families and want a role where you can make a lasting impact?

, the Regional Adoption Agency for Wolverhampton, Walsall, Dudley and Sandwell, is looking for a dedicated and compassionate Agency Family Support Worker to join our team.

This is a rewarding opportunity to work directly with children, young people, adoptive families, and birth families, providing vital support throughout their adoption journey. Every day brings the chance to help children build positive futures and support families through life-changing experiences.

About the Role

As an Agency Family Support Worker, you will play a key role in delivering practical and emotional support to children and families. Working as part of a supportive and experienced team, you will help children prepare for adoption, facilitate family contact arrangements, undertake life story work, and contribute to meaningful support plans that improve outcomes for children and families.

You will work across a range of settings, including family homes, community locations, offices, and group environments, building positive relationships and helping families navigate their adoption journey with confidence.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide direct support to children, young people, adoptive families, and birth families.
- Prepare children for adoption and support them through transition arrangements.
- Undertake life story work and create high-quality Life Story Books.
- Support post-adoption contact arrangements, including Letterbox and direct contact sessions.
- Plan, facilitate, and supervise individual and group support sessions.
- Contribute to assessments of adoption support needs and help develop support plans.
- Deliver support groups, training workshops, and family-focused interventions.
- Work closely with social workers, schools, health professionals, and other partner agencies.
- Maintain accurate records, case notes, and written reports, including court statements where required.
- Attend professional meetings and contribute to multi-agency planning and decision-making.
- Support service development and continuous improvement initiatives.

What We're Looking For

We're seeking someone who can demonstrate:
- Experience working with children, young people, and families.
- A genuine passion for improving outcomes for children.
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
- The ability to work sensitively with families from diverse backgrounds.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage a varied workload.
- Confidence in recording information accurately and producing written reports.
- The ability to work independently while contributing positively to a team.
- A flexible and proactive approach to supporting service needs.
- An understanding of safeguarding, child-centred practice, and professional boundaries.

Why Join ?

At children and families are at the centre of everything we do. This role offers the opportunity to be part of a service that genuinely changes lives and supports children in achieving the best possible outcomes.

In return, you'll benefit from:
- Flexible hybrid working arrangements.
- Meaningful and rewarding work with children and families.
- A supportive and collaborative team environment.
- Ongoing training and professional development opportunities.
- The chance to contribute to a respected regional adoption service.
- A varied role where no two days are the same.

Interested?

If you're a compassionate, resilient, and motivated professional who wants to make a positive difference to the lives of adopted children and their families, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today and help us continue to put children and families at the heart of every decision.

title: Residential Support Worker
description:
Are you an experienced Residential Support Worker looking for flexible agency work?

We are currently recruiting experienced and reliable Residential Support Workers to support vulnerable children and young people across a range of residential care settings.

The young people you will support may have experienced trauma or difficult life circumstances and may present with challenging behaviours, autism, emotional and behavioural difficulties and complex support needs.

This is a rewarding opportunity for caring and resilient individuals who want to make a positive difference while enjoying the flexibility of agency work.

The Role

As a Residential Support Worker, you will provide high-quality care and support to children and young people, helping them feel safe, supported and valued.

Your responsibilities may include:
- Providing day-to-day care and support to vulnerable children and young people
- Building positive and trusting relationships
- Supporting young people with their daily routines and individual needs
- Engaging children in activities, hobbies and interests
- Supporting emotional wellbeing and personal development
- Managing and responding appropriately to challenging behaviours
- Supporting children with autism and other additional needs
- Following individual care plans and risk assessments
- Maintaining professional boundaries and providing consistent support

Every shift will be different, and you may work with young people with a range of needs and backgrounds. You will need to be adaptable, patient and able to remain calm and professional in challenging situations.

Flexible Agency Shifts

Agency work gives you the flexibility to work around your existing commitments, with shifts available across a range of residential childcare settings.

You must be able to work flexible hours, which may include long day shifts, weekends, bank holidays and sleep ins. Flexibility is essential, as shift patterns and requirements will vary depending on the home and the needs of the young people.

About You

We are looking for people who are:
- Calm and emotionally resilient
- Confident supporting children with challenging behaviours
- Comfortable working with children and young people with autism and additional needs
- Reliable and professional
- Able to adapt to different care environments
- Passionate about making a positive difference in the lives of vulnerable young people

Requirements

To be considered for these agency opportunities, you will need:
- To be 21 years of age or over
- At least 6 months' experience working with children or young people in a residential setting
- A clean UK driving licence
- The flexibility to work long days, weekends and sleep-in shifts when required
- A genuine commitment to working with vulnerable children and young people

Why Work With Us?
- Flexible temporary agency shifts
- Opportunity to work across a variety of residential childcare settings
- Gain experience working with children with a range of complex needs
- Build your experience within the residential childcare sector
- Potential opportunities for ongoing and permanent work
- Support from your dedicated recruitment team
- Opportunity to make a genuine difference to vulnerable young people's lives

If you're an experienced Residential Support Worker looking for flexible agency work and are passionate about supporting children and young people, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today to discuss available shifts and opportunities in your area.
